quote.text: We abuse land because we regard it as a commodity belonging to us. When we see land as a community to which we belong, we may begin to use it with love and respect.
quote.author: Aldo Leopold, A Sand County Almanac (Oxford University Press, 1949), Foreword, p. viii

stories.headline: Teenage Engineering puts the compact disc on top, for US$329
stories.dek: The Stockholm firm’s first CD player, the EP/BC-1, went on sale on 20 November: the disc spins in plain sight, with a speed dial, Bluetooth and a battery.

stories.headline: Shin Jin-seo beats the Go engine KataGo at two stones
stories.dek: The Korean world No. 1 won the Seoul series 2–1 on 21 July 2026, ten years after AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4–1; some 20 million people still play.

stories.headline: Singapore Airlines swaps KrisFlyer upgrades for miles discounts
stories.dek: From 1 January the 75,000 and 100,000 Elite-mile upgrades become 10,000- and 20,000-mile discounts; Solitaire members’ yearly ceiling falls from 15 upgrades to five.

stories.kicker: The World · Myanmar At The Hague
stories.headline: World Court finds Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
stories.dek: The International Court of Justice split nine to six on 19 November, its first such finding against a state in 80 years. Naypyitaw called it unfair; Beijing objected the next day.

stories.headline: Singapore and China open talks on fourth trade-pact upgrade
stories.dek: Lawrence Wong and Xi Jinping launched the “4.0” negotiations in Shenzhen on 20 November, covering digital trade and public tenders, with no timetable and no text yet.

stories.headline: HOPPE’s Amsterdam lever prints its 200,000-turn test grade
stories.dek: HOPPE’s December 2025 data sheet codes the stainless set 37-0140A; Croft’s unlacquered solid-brass Crest lever sells at £259.25 a pair and prints no grade at all.

stories.headline: Nvidia sinks 14% as its Wall Street rout runs seven weeks
stories.dek: The shares ended Friday 20 November at 125.53 dollars, about 46 per cent below where the streak began, with Colette Kress still interim chief executive.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · Phillips Hong Kong Watch Auction
stories.headline: Phillips auctions 1952 Patek 2499 in Hong Kong today
stories.dek: Lot 958, a yellow-gold first series in a Wenger case off the market for 37 years, closes Saturday’s 11am session in West Kowloon, estimated at HK$12–24 million.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · Sunrise on the Reaping
stories.headline: Sunrise on the Reaping takes $21 million in previews
stories.dek: Lionsgate’s Hunger Games prequel, out in America on 20 November, now looks set for the studio’s first US$100 million opening since 2015; critics give it 67 per cent, audiences 95.

stories.kicker: Raising Them Well · Phones And Teenage Sleep
stories.headline: Stony Brook links teens’ bedtime phones to shorter sleep
stories.dek: Stony Brook University metered the phones of 218 American 13-to-18-year-olds for 17.5 days on average; the sleep cost of evening use was steepest in girls, the Journal of Adolescent Health reported on 6 November.

stories.headline: S&P 500 sinks into correction as Treasuries rally hard
stories.dek: On Friday 20 November the index fell 3.7 per cent, its seventh loss in a row and almost 9 per cent on the week, while the ten-year Treasury yield dropped to 4.92 per cent.

stories.headline: Hard cardio cuts visceral fat most, Shandong review finds
stories.dek: Deng and colleagues pooled 78 trial reports and 4,930 adults in Obesity Reviews on 10 November; the best weekly dose landed near 750 MET-minutes.

stories.kicker: The Diary · Snow Festival, YOASOBI And Sumo
stories.headline: Sapporo Snow Festival posts its 4–11 February 2027 dates
stories.dek: YOASOBI plays Singapore’s National Stadium on 20 February from S$108; Tokyo’s January sumo tickets go on sale on 5 December.

stories.headline: Tanners in Australia turn culled foxes and rabbits into fashion
stories.dek: Tanner Heidi Beynon sells pest pelts at an oddities expo that drew a record 2,000 Australian applicants this year — and a pest that pays, history warns, is a pest somebody keeps.
